title: Smyth’s Theorem in Lean — The Plastic Number ρ as a Sharp Lower Bound for Mahler Measure
abstract: In every degree, an integer polynomial with nonzero constant coefficient whose reverse differs from both it and its negative has multiplicative Mahler measure at least the plastic number. The cubic x³ − x − 1 attains the bound. In the compositum of its root and a root of x⁴ − x − 1, the least Mahler measure of an algebraic integer other than 0 and ±1 equals the plastic number. Each element uses its own minimal polynomial over ℤ. We also deduce Siegel’s theorem that the plastic number is the smallest Pisot number.
